kind: Manual Android emulator UI exercise with a real Chromium WebRTC peer

android.build: Custom native development build; Expo Go is unsupported

isolation: Disposable PostgreSQL and Redis; fictional rider/driver; synthetic stationary location and camera sources. Original emulator encrypted login/preferences/database restored afterward.

checks.name: Connected native/browser audio with bidirectional RTP and connected DTLS
Switch to video visible on connected Android audio call
Native requests upgrade, browser explicitly accepts, same call ID carries audio/video in both directions
Native remote video renders and local preview displays
Native camera flip retains connected media and decoded frames
Camera off returns shared call to audio
Incoming/sent messages and unsent draft retained after leaving/reopening chat
End closes browser peer and server call

manualFixtureNote: The live fixture was kept open across the interactive session and exceeded its 20-minute node:test timeout. It is not counted as a passing automated test. Media/UI observations and snapshots are separate manual evidence. End/stop endpoints were called, disposable resources closed, and the original emulator login restored.
remaining: Physical Android/iPhone microphone and speaker quality, Bluetooth and background/lock behavior
First-grant permission dialog flow on physical devices
